name: Jongmin Choi
title: MS Student in KAIST
university: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST)
bio: ***What computational principles enable the brain to learn and reason so efficiently?*** I am Jongmin Choi, an MS student in the [Multimodal AI (MMAI) Lab](https://mm.kaist.ac.kr/) at KAIST, advised by Professor [Joon Son Chung](https://mm.kaist.ac.kr/joon/). This question has shaped how I approach learning and model architecture. The brain processes different sensory inputs through specialized neural circuits, yet integrates them through recurrent interactions. I believe that drawing on such computational principles is as important as scaling up model capacity. Motivated by this perspective, I have studied audio–text representation learning that bridges the modality gap while preserving modality-specific structure, as well as temporal dynamics in spiking neural networks. I am now particularly interested in looped Transformers and Neural Cellular Automata (NCA), exploring recurrent computation and self-organization as potential principles for building more efficient and flexible neural architectures.
